gauntlet.intent: victory-trigger-conditional (T5 theme recipe, tierMin 5, precondition mission.triggers-supported): first candidate in this run where the mission.triggers CONDITION ITSELF is the objective-selector, not just a static ROE/scoring tweak. Confirmed by reading src/ProjectAegis.Data/Catalog/GauntletOracleExpect.cs and src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Projection/LossesScoringProjection.cs before drafting: there is still no dedicated victory-condition/objective field anywhere in the schema or scoring code (score = baseScore + kills*100 - denials*5, exactly as in the tier-4 victory-weighted-multi winner data/scenarios/gauntlet-forge-20260727-1455-t4-c3.policy.json) -- that candidate made SCORING multi-term but the weights were fixed for the whole run; this one makes which unit group is even doing anything meaningful DEPEND on a mid-run detection event. BLUE (9 units: surface f-219-sachsen-type-f124-2006/f-310-fridtjof-nansen/p-960-skjold, air jas-39e-gripen-ng-2021/eurofighter-typhoon/ka-27m-helix-a/p-3c-orion-update-iii-2023, subsurface ssn-774-virginia-blk-i-ii/s-120-papanikolis-type-214hn) starts entirely WeaponsTight -- a pure defensive-denial posture. The ASW hunter group (p-3c-orion-update-iii-2023, ka-27m-helix-a, ssn-774-virginia-blk-i-ii, s-120-papanikolis-type-214hn) is deliberately GATED with no tasking of its own: it only escalates to WeaponsFree via trigger 'hvu-detected-objective-shift', which fires on p-3c-orion-update-iii-2023's first Unknown->Detected classification of RED's flagship/HVU plarb-955-borei-borey (the tier-5-roster.json-flagged 'primary ASW high-value target'). If that detection had not happened, that whole 4-unit group would sit WeaponsTight/denied for all 40 ticks and the run's practical objective would just be the same denial posture enforced by the permanently-untriggered surface pair (f-310-fridtjof-nansen, p-960-skjold, deliberately given no ASuW trigger at all, same pattern as t4-c3's 'no ASuW trigger' surface group) plus the separate always-on 'aaw-defensive-intercept-baseline' trigger (f-219-sachsen-type-f124-2006 vs Air contacts, freeing f-219-sachsen-type-f124-2006/jas-39e-gripen-ng-2021/eurofighter-typhoon once any RED aircraft is classified Detected). Because this run needs a checkable oracle across seeds 42/7/123, the HVU detection entry (observerId p-3c-orion-update-iii-2023, contactId c-t5c4-hvu-detect) is deliberately set to basePd 1.0 so the 'detected -> objective becomes destroy-the-HVU' branch is the one deterministically taken here; the counterfactual 'never detected -> stays pure denial' branch is mechanically supported by the identical code path (MissionContactTriggerRuntime never fires the trigger if the Unknown->Detected transition never occurs) but is NOT exercised or fingerprint-gated by this specific candidate -- demonstrating it would need a sibling candidate with a sub-1.0 basePd or an omitted detection entry, out of scope for this single-file candidate. RED (9 units: subsurface plarb-955-borei-borey [SSBN flagship/HVU] + pla-885m-severodvinsk-yasen-m [SSGN escort], surface skr-admiral-grigorovich-pr-1135-6m/pk-368-vasily-bykov-pr-22160/mrk-shkval-pr-22800-karakurt, air su-35s-flanker-m-2023/su-57-felon/tu-160-blackjack/mig-31-foxhound) stays WeaponsTight throughout with no triggers of its own -- a defensive screen around its own SSBN, same convention as t4-c3, so only BLUE is scored (gauntlet.expect.side = BLUE). Genuine schema-gap finding made while drafting (not present in the task's reading list, found by reading the actual trigger runtime code before writing targetClass values): src/ProjectAegis.Sim/Scenario/MissionContactTargetClass.cs defines only Any/Surface/Air -- there is NO Subsurface enum member -- and ScenarioPolicyJsonLoader.ParseMissionContactTargetClass (src/ProjectAegis.Sim/Scenario/ScenarioPolicyJsonLoader.cs:362-365) silently falls back to Any via Enum.TryParse whenever it is given an unrecognized label. Both precedent candidates this task pointed to as reference (tier-3/scenario-1.policy.json's 'asw-contact-roe' trigger and tier-4's t4-c3 'asw-prosecution-roe' trigger) authored \"targetClass\": \"Subsurface\" and, per this code, silently got Any (i.e. their ASW triggers actually fire on ANY first-Detected contact from their observerId, not specifically a subsurface one) -- this almost certainly did not change their observed behavior in practice (each observer there had only one detection entry, so Any vs a notional Subsurface filter is a no-op), but it is a latent authoring mistake worth flagging back into the corpus/bug tracker rather than silently repeating. CORRECTION (post-draft review): the second trigger, aaw-defensive-intercept-baseline, was originally authored with "targetClass": "Air" on the mistaken assumption that a syntactically-valid enum member was automatically safe -- it was not. MissionContactTargetClassifier.Classify(targetId) only ever returns Air when targetId literally starts with "ucav" (src/ProjectAegis.Sim/Scenario/MissionContactTargetClass.cs:12-15); tu-160-blackjack does not, so Classify() returns Surface and Matches(Air, tu-160-blackjack) == (Surface == Air) is always false. Unlike the Subsurface case (which harmlessly falls back to Any), an explicit Air targetClass does NOT fall back -- it is evaluated literally, and since Classify() never actually returns Air for any real catalog platform id in this corpus, the trigger would have NEVER fired despite its own always-on intent and despite the underlying detection (basePd 1.0) resolving deterministically every run. Caught and fixed before finalizing: targetClass corrected to Any (same safe pattern as the hvu trigger -- correctness does not depend on the filter since f-219-sachsen-type-f124-2006 has exactly one detection entry, targeting only tu-160-blackjack). Both this Air-never-matches finding and the Subsurface-silently-becomes-Any finding are the same underlying targetClass parsing/matching gap and are filed together. This candidate's hvu trigger explicitly declares \"targetClass\": \"Any\" (matching its actual runtime behavior honestly) instead of copying the same 'Subsurface' typo forward; correctness here does not depend on the class filter at all since p-3c-orion-update-iii-2023 has exactly one detection entry (targeting only plarb-955-borei-borey) in this policy, so 'first Detected transition from this observer' is already flagship-specific by construction. contacts[] deliberately not used anywhere in this candidate (BUG-scenario-contacts-shadowed-by-detection: contacts[]/ScenarioContactSimulator is dead on arrival whenever detection[] is non-empty, per BalticReplayHarness.RunCore's if/else-if branch) -- all mid-run contact appearance is expressed through detection[] basePd rolls exclusively, the confirmed-working mechanism.
gauntlet.oracle: The trigger IS the objective-selector: gauntlet.expect.requireFingerprintSubstrings checks for the two trigger IDs verbatim -- 'hvu-detected-objective-shift' and 'aaw-defensive-intercept-baseline' -- because MissionContactTriggerRuntime.Evaluate (src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Mission/MissionContactTriggerRuntime.cs) firing is logged by BalticReplayHarness (src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter/Baltic/BalticReplayHarness.cs:409-416) as a real MissionTransition order-log entry, EventId=trigger.TriggerId, PhaseCode=trigger.MissionCode; DecisionLog.ComputeFingerprint's FormatPayload (src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Decision/DecisionLog.cs:288-289) renders that as the literal token '{SimTick}|{TriggerId}|{MissionCode}' inside the MissionTransition-kind fingerprint line. This is the real, code-native 'trigger fired' marker -- not an invented schema field. Requiring both trigger IDs present proves (a) the conditional HVU-detection branch was actually taken this run (the ASW hunter group's tasking really did shift to hunt-the-flagship) and (b) the always-on AAW defensive-denial baseline also engaged, regardless of the branch outcome. Each trigger's per-unit ROE rebind additionally leaves its own 'roe'-field PolicyUpdate entries in the log (DelegationOrchestrator.ApplyRoeToUnits, confirmed by src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter.Tests/Baltic/BalticReplayHarnessTheaterPolicyTests.cs's own comment 'Contact-triggered ROE rebind leaves PolicyUpdate in the log') as a secondary, non-gated confirmation signal not asserted here to keep the oracle to the same 2-substring shape as t4-c3's precedent. Composite score is exactly kills*100 - denials*5 per LossesScoringProjection.Project, same formula as every other candidate this run -- no new scoring mechanism is introduced, only the objective/tasking structure that determines which units are even allowed to contribute kills changes mid-run.
